answer.answer: Field brief: Little Cloud is a modest 2/5 threat, but you are carrying enough valuable ammunition and consumables that a quick storage run is worthwhile. If banking is inconvenient, clear it methodically and keep replacement gear near the tagged chamber. The chamber shortens the return trip; it does not preserve or replace lost equipment, and corruption has previously disabled a claimed chamber. Starry Night is easier—about 1/5—with no persistent hostile markers nearby, although roamers can intrude. Clear them, open the final chest first, then loot debris.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty. Within 250 units it has 13 persistent hostile spawn entries: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder, with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers indicate possible persistent population, not 13 simultaneous attackers. The player later completed the site and reported it was “no big deal,” but that historical observation does not erase the mapped threat.

Protect the carried supplies by banking excess ammunition and consumables when storage is reasonably quick. Otherwise proceed methodically, treating the nearby Regeneration Chamber as travel insurance while keeping replacement equipment and a safe recovery cache available.

A nearby claimed Regeneration Chamber can shorten the return after death, but it does not provide spare weapons or replacement materials; Update 1 makes carried weapons losable on death, so corpse recovery and cached replacement gear still matter. Historical field evidence also records corruption disabling a contested base and its claimed chamber, after which the player respawned at the starting launcher. The exact corruption threshold and any universal Regeneration Chamber rule remain unverified, so that observed failure must not be generalized into a definitive mechanic.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty, with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, though roaming enemies can still wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains the Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module. Clear wanderers, open that chest first, then loot the debris.

claims.value: Grand Basin Reserve is north of the active Landerworks–Faraday corridor and immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry,” which lies in the mountains at approximately `2518.767,3099.107`. The Grand Basin marker identifies the basin area rather than a future Core; the proposed first campus belongs east of Mythic Cry on the basin side of the terrain boundary.

The preferred first permanent Goethite satellite is the safer northwestern triple at approximately `1393–1464,1838–1891`, northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin. It is preferred because the closer western field around `1252–1472,2950–3282` overlaps scanner/hostile envelopes. The adopted proposal after Engine access and Selenian 9 is three Laser Drills merged locally into one Goethite-only Cargo Dispatcher, delivering 45 raw Ore/min to one Receiver and a 1,600-unit Storage Depot v2; the geographically separate fourth drill is only an empty-buffer fallback and requires another Dispatcher/Receiver pair. The preferred first Oil satellite is approximately `1234,3760`, west/southwest of Mythic Cry and Grand Basin. The adopted proposal after Future Health 11 is one Oil Extractor and one Crude-only Dispatcher/Receiver pair delivering 10 Crude/min through one V2 buffer to one GB-A Refinery. A second pair and Refinery are reserved but not initially built because one Refinery consumes the full 10 Crude/min source plus large Titanium and Calcium feeds; the marker around `1351,4473` is a separate site. These are adopted plans, not verified installed satellites. Raw resources are shipped because Goethite and Crude Oil are compact at extraction and expand during processing; each resource keeps its own Cargo link, rail lane, and storage unit, with processing beside Grand Basin consumers.

answer.answer: The Watch Session design is evidence-bounded and ready for MVP modeling, but not for claims of exact synchronization or guaranteed safety. It centers the interface on the next meaningful player event, represents opportunities independently from cycle phases, and uses conservative confidence, accessible alerts, and explicit native-iOS capability rules.

claims.value: The design is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620, released 2026-06-17, with SRDB 2.3.4 captured 2026-07-11. The 54-minute interval from local fire-wave impact to the next local impact is a strongly corroborated community/game-data model, not an official formula or eternal invariant. Manual sessions must expose Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, and Cycle data changed - re-sync required. Confidence must be downgraded after a large correction, device-clock or model-version change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop. Until Hotfix 0.2.8 cycles are validated across solo, hosted co-op, and dedicated servers, use predicted, expected, favorable, and lower threat—never exact, safe, or guaranteed.

claims.value: Preserve the 54-minute engine model while presenting five player-facing states: Fire wave 0:00-0:30 (Remain sheltered), Cooling 0:30-1:30 (Remain sheltered), Recovery / quiet window 1:30-11:30 (Lower ambient threat; use the window), World active 11:30-51:30 (Ordinary enemies and ecology active), and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00 (Return, bank loot, and shelter). Sync 0:00 when the fire wall reaches the player. The portrait screen keeps five layers visible without scrolling: sync/capability status; a semantic hero state, across-the-room monospaced countdown, and explicit target; threat instruction and action sentence; at most two opportunity cards; then exact-time next events with Mute one cycle and Re-sync always visible. During recovery the hero counts down until ordinary Vermin are expected to return; during normal ecology it targets the next Ruptura or warning-phase start. Retain a proportional overview rail, but supplement it with minimum-width labeled steps or a next-event list so short Fire wave and Cooling phases remain legible.

claims.value: Opportunities are separately versioned evidence records, not automatic phase mechanics. Each OpportunityWindow carries an ID, start and end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. Initial candidates are: reduced ordinary POI population during Recovery with the warning that triggered encounters may persist; Oxallop during early recovery while lakebeds are dry; caves, Quartz, and Glowcaps during Recovery without guaranteed respawn; Ignitium immediately after Cooling through Recovery with variable spawn rate; experimentally timed Star Tears in late Recovery, including the choice to leave cooled Ignitium unharvested; variable Coralion/Vulpir egg opportunities after the wave; and broad foliage/water regrowth guidance during the active world rather than species-level timers. Hide Sulheart until its exact current timing is validated. Triggered Geo Scanner, monolith, infection, Base Core, scripted POI, and similar encounters can ignore the environmental cycle, so Recovery is only a lower-threat opportunity window.

claims.value: Enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptic signatures, with text, symbols, borders or patterns so neither color nor audio stands alone. The proposed enemy-return ladder is 5 minutes (amber edge, finish/leave hard POIs, short double haptic, optional tone, normal notification), 2 minutes (persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, optional notification), 1 minute (red instruction and emphasized seconds, stronger cue, background alert off by default), 15 seconds (static danger border, large seconds, one final cue without ticking), and the event (ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING, urgent triple cue, local notification or explicitly armed alarm). Ruptura supports optional 10-minute planning, then 5 minutes, 2:30 warning start, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact; a player-selected exit buffer may issue TURN BACK NOW earlier. Provide Full, Haptic only, and Visual only profiles, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, preview, Mute one cycle, and no replayed backlog after resume—collapse missed cues to the strongest current-state message. Store absolute timestamps, recompute `(now - anchor) modulo cycle duration` on resume, reschedule notifications after anchor/model/policy changes, and deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor is active and restore it; never use background audio as keep-alive. Use a Live Activity only for the currently armed event. On iOS 26, AlarmKit may break through Silent mode and Focus only after explicit player arming and authorization; never silently schedule endless 54-minute alarms. Earlier iOS uses normal local notifications, Time Sensitive is opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Preserve Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, stable VoiceOver summaries, no full-screen flashing, and no default per-second ticking.

claims.value: Alert and native-iOS safety rules: enemy return and Ruptura require distinct sounds and haptics, while every cue also has visual/text treatment. Enemy-return defaults are 5 minutes, 2 minutes, 1 minute, 15 seconds, and event; pre-Ruptura defaults are optional 10 minutes, 5 minutes, warning start at 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Schedule ordinary local notifications at absolute dates and display permission/capability state. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor is active and restore it afterward; never use background audio as keep-alive. A Live Activity represents only the currently armed event, not an indefinitely self-advancing promise. iOS 26 AlarmKit may break through Silent/Focus only after explicit player arming and authorization; never create an endless 54-minute alarm.
